In service diagnostics, `lumbar_summary.detected` counts levels with a native `LUM_Ln_COM` landmark.
Segmentation-only levels are reported as `seg_only` and cannot supply the registration center. The
center is the lower-middle of the sorted landmark-confirmed levels (index `(n - 1) // 2`); for
example, L1–L4 selects `LUM_L2_COM`.

operations.old_text:
## Server payload

The 3D annotation server accepts the same controls in `submit_job` payloads:

See the [service contract](service.md) for launch, polling, shared-filesystem paths,
and returned-output ownership. The example below
explicitly enables destructive overwrite; use `false` to preserve an existing
case output. Inspect artifacts under the returned `result.annotation_output_dir`,
which may be a nested case directory.

```json
{
  "type": "submit_job",
  "input_path": "/path/to/input.nii.gz",
  "project_dir": "/path/to/xreg_project",
  "overwrite_existing": true,
  "device": "cpu",
  "fastest": true,
  "body_seg": true,
  "force_split": true,
  "roi_subset": [
    "hip_left",
    "hip_right",
    "femur_left",
    "femur_right",
    "vertebrae_L1",
    "vertebrae_L2",
    "vertebrae_L3",
    "vertebrae_L4",
    "vertebrae_L5",
    "vertebrae_S1",
    "sacrum"
  ]
}
```

The job snapshot and `source_input.json` record `device`, `fastest`,
`body_seg`, `force_split`, and `roi_subset` so each run is auditable.
